title: The two normalized geometric fibres of a classical lisse realization agree
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and write $g_Y$ for geometric Frobenius. Use the classical lisse adic categories of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], the sf raw rationalized and common-stage constructible hearts of [def-weil-constructible-heart, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and the normalized lisse realization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$. Let $N=(N_n)_{n\geq1}$ be a normalized finite locally free $A/\varpi^n$ etale sheaf system on $Y$, with locally constant finite rank, and set $\widehat N=\varprojlim_n\nu_Y^*N_n$ and $E_Y=(\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_Y)[1/\varpi]$. Let $K$ be a lisse sf finite-stage heart object with its specified normalized realization isomorphism to $\widehat N[1/\varpi]$ in degree zero. Under the comparison $J_{Y,E}$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], the sf and PBC finite-stage hearts are identified, and the continuous derived realization of $J_{Y,E}K$ is isomorphic to $(\widehat N[1/\varpi])[0]$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},E_Y)$. For every geometric point $\bar y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to Y$, there are compatible natural isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*K)\cong V_{\bar y}(N):=\bigl(\varprojlim_n(N_n)_{\bar y}\bigr)\otimes_AE\cong\omega_{\bar y,E}(J_{Y,E}K),$$
where the left functor is [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and the right functor is [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness]. The inverse-limit module is finite free over $A$. For an integral system map $f=(f_n):N\to N'$ divided by $\varpi^t$, both isomorphisms carry the induced map to $\varpi^{-t}(\varprojlim_n(f_n)_{\bar y})\otimes_AE$. The comparisons are independent of the fractional representative, are compatible with finite coefficient extension $E\subset E'$ and scalar extension to $\Omega$, and are natural for maps between the realized objects. They include rank zero and varying ranks on finitely many clopen components.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; normalized geometric pullback, point sections, and the sf/PBC heart comparison. Agent refinement for blueprint real-mixed-by-curves paragraph 1.

proof.text: First check the schemes needed by the comparisons. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. A field is noetherian, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applied to the finite-type structure map makes $Y$ locally noetherian; finite type includes quasi-compactness, hence $Y$ is noetherian. It has finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], and $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. These assertions also hold for $s$. The equivalence [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] is the identity on the common integral objects and on $u\otimes e$. The nonpositive and nonnegative classes in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] and [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] are the isomorphism closures of precisely the same integral cohomological classes. Thus $J_{Y,E}$ identifies their intersections, namely the two hearts. By [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] its continuous realization on an integral representative $C$ is $E_Y\otimes^L_{B_Y}C$, with $B_Y=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_Y$. This is also the functor defining [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization], including its arrow formula. The specified realization of $K$ therefore gives the claimed isomorphism $\operatorname{Real}(J_{Y,E}K)\cong\widehat N[1/\varpi][0]$ in the ambient derived category.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; common integral identity and standard cohomological classes

proof.text: By [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison], $\widehat N$ is a lisse $B_Y$-module with reduction system exactly $(N_n)$. The given normalized realization therefore supplies an actual integral lisse lattice of the continuous sheaf representing $J_{Y,E}K$. Apply [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness] on any affine etale neighbourhood of $\bar y$, taking this lattice restricted to that neighbourhood. Its normalization identifies $\omega_{\bar y,E}(J_{Y,E}K)$ with $M_{\bar y}\otimes_AE$, where $M_{\bar y}=\varprojlim_n(N_n)_{\bar y}$, and asserts that $M_{\bar y}$ is finite free. The chart-independent identification of that lemma applies to this chosen global lattice, so this gives the right-hand comparison without choosing a different lattice or a path between points.

Pull the system $(N_n)$ to $s$ along $\bar y$. Put $P=\varprojlim_n\nu_s^*(\bar y^{-1}N_n)$. The pullback compatibility in [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] identifies $P$ with the ordinary module pullback of $\widehat N$. At finite level [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the pulled fibre with $(N_n)_{\bar y}$, sending every pulled germ to the original germ and commuting with each transition and each $f_n$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed its absolute Galois group is trivial. The equivalence [lem-exc-etale-sheaves-gsets-point], applied also to the module structure maps, identifies the pulled etale sheaf with the constant module of its fibre. That fibre is finite free over $A/\varpi^n$. Inverse image to the pro-etale site preserves constant coefficient sheaves and finite sums, so a basis identifies its pro-etale pullback with a finite sum of $(A/\varpi^n)_s$. By [lem-pur-proetale-finite-constant-sections] the sections of each coefficient summand at $s$ are $A/\varpi^n$, with the constant-section normalization. Hence its sections are canonically $(N_n)_{\bar y}$; changing bases changes both sides by the same matrix. The inverse-limit construction [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] is sectionwise. Consequently $\Gamma(s,P)=M_{\bar y}$, and a pulled system map has sections map exactly $\varprojlim_n(f_n)_{\bar y}$. This calculation pulls the normalized system first; it does not commute an arbitrary geometric stalk with an infinite limit.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), Remark 6.8.15, Lemma 4.2.12; Stacks Tags 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback (3)) and 03QT (theorem-equivalence-sheaves-point)

proof.text: The pullback and point normalization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] carries $L\bar y^*K$ to $P[1/\varpi][0]$. Here $P[0]$ belongs to the common integral constructible category by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]: its lisse local model is a finite free module in degree zero. Realization also carries the rationalized integral lattice $P[0]$ to that same sheaf. Full faithfulness lifts this specified identification to an isomorphism of the two rationalized objects: lift the sheaf isomorphism and its inverse, and their composites are identities by faithfulness. The point functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], applied to $P[0]$, is $\Gamma(s,P)\otimes_AE$ in degree zero; exact sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] justifies this use on the derived category. The preceding computation gives $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*K)\cong(M_{\bar y}\otimes_AE)[0]$. This is the left-hand comparison, with vector spaces in the displayed statement understood in degree zero. It is normalized by the same quotient projections as the right-hand comparison.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; specified pullback/point realization and definition of the point functor

proof.text: For $f/\varpi^t$, step 3 gives the integral point map $\varprojlim_n(f_n)_{\bar y}$. The localized arrow prescription in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] multiplies it by $\varpi^{-t}$; the normalized prescription in [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-exactness] gives exactly the same formula on the right. The equivalence [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] changes neither the integral map nor this scalar. Hence both squares commute. If $f/\varpi^t=h/\varpi^u$, equality in a localized Hom module means that $\varpi^b(\varpi^uf-\varpi^th)=0$ for some $b$. Apply each finite-level fibre map and then take the limit: the same equality holds for limit maps, and inversion of $\varpi$ makes the rational maps equal. Finally [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] is fully faithful after raw localization. Therefore every map between the realized sheaves with the specified lattices is represented by such a fraction. The formulas prove naturality for every map between the realized objects, not merely maps for which an integral representative was initially supplied.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(4), localized Hom and fractional-map prescriptions

proof.text: For $E\subset E'$, use the scalar system of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]: its level $m$ is $N_{n(m)}\otimes_{A/\varpi^{n(m)}}A'/\varpi'^m$, where $n(m)=\lceil m/e\rceil$ and $e$ is the ramification index. The pullback and scalar comparisons of [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] are induced by these quotient maps. The scalar comparison of [lem-per-adic-normalized-fibre-comparisons] identifies its rational limit fibre with $M_{\bar y}\otimes_AE'$, using those same finite integral maps. On the sf side [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] respects finite coefficient extension with its specified normalization, and [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] identifies the sf and PBC scalar functors with their associators. Thus the comparison constructed above commutes with extension to $E'$: on every quotient the two routes send a pulled germ tensored with a scalar to that same germ tensored with that scalar. Equality after every quotient gives equality into the inverse limit, and localization gives the required rational square. For successive extensions both routes multiply the scalars, so these squares respect the associators. Passing to the common finite-stage description gives the comparison after scalar extension to $\Omega$, including naturality in common-stage maps.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Proposition 6.8.14; finite scalar and common-stage normalizations

proof.text: All formulas use the actual normalized lattice, its quotient projections and its map on germs. On a clopen component of rank $r$ they compute $M_{\bar y}\cong A^r$ and $V_{\bar y}(N)\cong E^r$. For $r=0$ these are zero modules and the same formulas are their unique maps. Restriction to any of the finitely many clopen rank components leaves every construction and displayed formula unchanged. The empty scheme has no geometric points, so its fibre assertions are vacuous. Thus no nonzero-rank or connectedness assumption has been inserted.
